hero.narrative_lead: Byron Sigcho Lopez is fighting to give IL-04
hero.narrative_run: Learn more about how democracy was subverted, and how a people-power movement is fighting back.
hero.context: The movement delivered. Byron needed 10,816 valid signatures to appear on your November 3rd ballot. Volunteers collected and filed 22,788, more than double the requirement. The machine's handpicked candidate needed just 697. Now machine lawyers have filed an objection (June 9, 2026) with the Illinois State Board of Elections to throw out your signatures and kick Byron off the ballot. They had their coronation on March 17th, when IL-04 voters had only ONE choice. We won't let them erase your voice in November. Let the people decide.

bio.label: Meet Byron
bio.headline: Byron Sigcho Lopez is a father of triplets and an independent socialist organizer fighting to make Illinois work for you.
bio.p1: Byron is an immigrant who came to the United States alone when he was 17 years old. His life is a testament to what happens when strangers become neighbors and family.
bio.p2: Byron Sigcho Lopez is the only elected official in this race who has delivered material benefits for the working people of Chicagoland, with a record of coalition building with every neighbor willing to come together to solve the problems we face, together. He has courageously fought the corruption of the Illinois political machine, helping take down corrupt charter school networks looting from our children's future, and even taking campaign finance corruption all the way to the Illinois Supreme Court.
bio.p3: Byron earned his Bachelor's in Mathematics and Business Administration from Cumberland University and his Master's in Economics from the University of Illinois at Chicago.
bio.p4: Byron lives in the Pilsen neighborhood with his wife, Loreen, their 3-year-old triplets, a dog, and two cats.

anointment.label: Why Independent?
anointment.headline: The Anointment
anointment.text: When Rep. Jesús "Chuy" García announced his retirement, he didn't give voters a choice. He filed for a fifth term, then moments before the filing deadline, his former chief of staff filed nominating petitions collected in just days. García withdrew and endorsed her, handing the seat to an uncontested successor. She needed only 697 signatures. Independent candidates must collect over 10,816. This is not democracy. This is an anointment. And when 22,788 voters signed petitions to put a choice on the ballot anyway, the machine's answer was to send lawyers: on June 9, 2026, a machine-backed objector filed a challenge to throw out your signatures. Don't elect their successor. Let the people decide.

meet.hero_badge: INDEPENDENT DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST • CHICAGO DSA • IL-04
meet.hero_sub: From Ecuador to Tennessee to Pilsen. Byron Sigcho-Lopez came to this country alone at 17 and has spent his life fighting alongside the working class as a teacher, researcher, organizer, and unapologetic democratic socialist.
meet.origin_p1: Byron first came to the United States alone as a teenager, settling in Tennessee and then moving to the Chicago area and Pilsen over 10 years ago. He was born and raised in Quito, Ecuador and came to the US following political instability in the country, and a tragic car accident that left his mother in a coma.
meet.origin_p2: Emergency services were nearly non-existent during this period, and his family's lives were saved by passing motorists who stopped, rescued his family from the wreckage, and drove them to the hospital. When his mother awoke from the coma, she insisted her eldest leave the country for his last year of high school.
meet.origin_p3: When Byron arrived in Tennessee at the age of 17, he knew no one in the country and did not speak English. He was taken in by a generous family who gave him a home and helped him pursue an education.
meet.education_p1: Byron first visited Chicago with his Tennessee family who had loved ones in the Chicago area. During this first trip, they brought Byron to Pilsen to have dinner at the Nuevo Leon restaurant.
meet.education_p2: After graduating high school in Tennessee, Byron was able to attend college on a soccer scholarship after receiving an honorable mention for the All-State Tennessee Soccer Team in high school. Byron graduated from Cumberland University with his Bachelors in Mathematics and Business Administration.
meet.education_p3: He was also awarded the prestigious President's Award for his exceptional academic performance, and many contributions and successes in the school community during his time there. After graduation, Byron returned to Chicago and eventually settled in Pilsen to start his life.
meet.record_desc: Byron became an adult education teacher at the University of Illinois at Chicago and founded the UIC Center for Literacy's Spanish literacy program, making the GED program at UIC much more widely accessible to Spanish speaking immigrants and residents. Seeing the need for wrap-around services, Byron also brought a case worker into the program to ensure his students' families received resources and needed services.
meet.record_desc2: In addition to Byron's work as a teacher, he also volunteered as a youth soccer coach at Pilsen Academy. Byron earned a Master's Degree in Economics from UIC while also working as a lead researcher. He began collaborating alongside the Chicago Teachers Union in investigating the financial relationships between charter school networks like UNO, school funding, and Chicago's political elite, and organized with parents and teachers like Karen Lewis to fight for fully funded public schools.
meet.schools_desc: After Rahm Emanuel announced that he would be closing a hundred thirty Chicago Public Schools, Byron became involved in the Pilsen Alliance where he organized with the community to push to keep the schools open.
meet.first_run_desc: In 2015, Byron was encouraged by community leaders Nellie Cotton and Kit Duffy to run for Alderman against the machine - now disgraced former Alderman Danny Solis. Byron came in second in the 5-way race.
meet.alliance_desc: Byron eventually served as the Director of Pilsen Alliance where he became a leader and an activist in the fight against gentrification, displacement, and corruption.
meet.dsa_desc: He joined forces with organizers from the Chicago Democratic Socialists of America as he was partnering on the coalition to Lift the Ban on Rent Control across the state of Illinois, and became a member then and there.
meet.elected_headline: A Grassroots Movement, Not a Machine Candidacy
meet.elected_p1: In 2019, Byron ran a grassroots campaign for Alderman of the 25th Ward. He committed to refuse political contributions from developers and big corporations - a commitment he has upheld to this day and beyond. Since taking office, any resident now can personally meet with Byron at his weekly Ward Night, and all residents can receive compassion, support, and city services from the devoted public servants who staff the 25th Ward office.
meet.elected_p2: In 2023, big money and the political establishment lined up against Byron. Byron took democratic establishment and corrupt Danny Solis all the way to the Illinois Supreme Court over his unethical campaign finance practices. The voters of the 25th Ward sent him back to City Hall.
meet.elected_p3: As an elected official, he used the power of his office to put the people's power into the institutions that needed it - under his leadership, change is happening.
meet.achieve_housing_desc: Byron has preserved and created over 800 units of affordable housing across Chicago and as Chairman of the Committee on Housing and Real Estate, made Chicago the largest city to pass a $135 million dollar investment via the Green Social Housing Initiative, to build sustainable housing and help address the housing crisis in Illinois.
meet.achieve_wardnight_desc: Every community member has the opportunity to speak directly with their elected official every Tuesday at the Ward Office - the accountability is a commitment.
meet.achieve_health_desc: The Pilsen Food Pantry has grown to serve more than ever. Perpetrators of heinous crimes are held accountable more often and public safety has become more possible for the community to organize for. A dental clinic accessible to the people was opened and a mental health clinic as well.
meet.achieve_fight_desc: Property tax payers know that their elected official has voted against every single proposed property tax increase, and worked to fight for a statewide millionaire surcharge and wealth taxes on the billionaires. When Trump sent ICE to our communities, Byron faced them head on with the full weight of his office and his community ensuring that Bovino and other thugs were held accountable to the furthest extent possible in court.
meet.elected_call: Byron has changed what was possible in public service on the municipal level and he isn't stopping. We need him in Congress.
meet.family_desc: Byron, and his wife Loreen, live in Pilsen with their little triplets (who attend public school), and their dog, Buster, and their two cats Dos and 三歲.

meet.caption_schools: Fighting for investment in our neighborhood schools

issues.hero_headline: A Platform for Working People, Not the Billionaire Class.
issues.hero_sub: Byron is fighting to guarantee a baseline standard of dignity for working families, seniors, teachers, and marginalized groups across IL-04.
issues.housing_title: Housing for every veteran and all our neighbors
issues.housing_desc: Between May of 2025 and April of 2026, more than 10,000 veterans lost their homes to foreclosure after the Trump regime shut down a key safety net in the VA home loan program - and 90,000 more veterans are at risk of foreclosure now.
issues.housing_desc2: Our country can and must provide dignified and safe housing for every veteran and neighbor who needs a helping hand. Byron will fight for a national tenant bill of rights and expanded social housing developments to lower the rent and lower the cost of buying a home.
issues.housing_desc3: He will bring his constituent services in partnership with community and labor organizing to build real power structures to bring compassion and intervention for everyone who is in need of housing dignity.
issues.healthcare_desc: Our resources are not endless and not one more dollar should go to greedy middlemen who do not improve the health of our people. Byron will organize for and pass Medicare for All, and exponentially grow our investment in the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to direct more of our most curious students and scientists towards spending their time eliminating and curing premature causes of death or chronic illnesses like heart disease, cancer, and mental illness. We must expand teaching hospitals and support for students from underserved communities to become healthcare workers, so we can eliminate maternal and infant mortality disparities including among our Black mothers and babies, and have improved health outcomes for all communities across IL-04.
issues.healthcare_desc2: Healthcare for all includes reproductive health care, abortion services, fertility treatments, elder care and home assistance, mental health support, and parental time off to ensure families are supported in every stage of life.
issues.economic_title: Green jobs. Local economies. A livable future.
issues.economic_desc: Our tax dollars have been misused by both political parties - on wars, on bailouts for banks and the tech bubble, for corporations that don't even pay taxes. Meanwhile the people in our neighborhoods who work every day never see their tax dollars they earned come back to serve their own future.
issues.economic_desc2: Byron will raise the tax rate on billionaires and invest our resources in our local economies, creating sustainable living-wage jobs for every worker in our communities. Raise the minimum wage to $30/hour. Investments in supporting local entrepreneurs that form the backbone of our economy across IL-04. Civilian climate corps jobs to invest in green energy projects, expansion of natural and recreational spaces, and resilience around storms, floods, heatwaves, and disasters in our communities. This will also include expanding green and public transportation options to increase pedestrian and commuter safety, and investing in renewable energy development so that we don't depend on fossil fuels to move from A to B.
issues.democracy_title: Democracy for the people, not for billionaires and corporations
issues.democracy_desc: Our democracy is supposed to work for all of us, but today it's rigged for those with the most money to the detriment of the soul of our nation. Billionaires and corporations pour millions into campaigns, lobbyists write legislation behind closed doors, and working families are left with the bill. Byron will never take a dime from corporate PACs or the political machine. In Congress, Byron will fight to end the influence of dark money, ban stock trading for members of Congress, pass automatic voter registration, make Election Day a national holiday, and restore the Voting Rights Act. Byron will forcefully pursue charges against the criminals in the Epstein Files. Democracy shouldn't be something the wealthy can buy. It should belong to every single one of us.
issues.immigration_desc: No human being is illegal. Byron will fight to abolish ICE and end the militarized deportation machine terrorizing our communities. He will ban ICE from operating on public property, shut down detention centers like the Wyatt Detention Center, and end the sale of surveillance data from Flock, Ring, and other systems to resist the consolidation of a surveillance state. He will create a clear, humane pathway to citizenship for the millions of neighbors who build our communities every day. And he will enforce accountability for police officers and demilitarize law enforcement.
issues.education_title: Literacy, Curiosity, Creativity, and Inspiration Now
issues.education_desc: Every student, 0–100, deserves the opportunity to be inspired, pursue their curiosity, nurture their creativity, and expand their literacy. Byron will fight to restore the U.S. Department of Education and the civil rights benefits for all learners. He will invest in fully funded public education based on student need and provide every student and family with robust wraparound services and extracurricular activities. As an adult education teacher, Byron supports education as a lifelong pursuit and will invest in education programs for all, beyond adolescence into adulthood.
issues.family_title: No-cost childcare and a strong start for every family
issues.family_desc: Byron is a former Head Start teacher and a father of triplets, so he knows both sides of this fight. Childcare in Chicagoland now costs as much as rent, and parents are holding down two and three jobs with barely enough time to breathe, let alone be with their children. The billionaire class has put a paywall on family life. Byron will fight for universal, no-cost childcare for every child from 6 weeks to 5 years old, and for wages that pay childcare workers, too many of whom live in poverty today, at parity with public school teachers.
issues.family_desc2: Byron will also fight to guarantee paid family leave, restore the expanded Child Tax Credit that cut child poverty nearly in half before Washington let it expire, and bring home federal investment for newborn essentials: diapers, wipes, swaddles, books, and a guide of resources for every new parent, modeled on more than 90 baby basket programs around the world. Every family in IL-04 deserves a baseline standard of dignity, where parents have time to help with homework and make their kids feel safe and loved, and where everybody has a home and everybody eats.
issues.foreignpolicy_title: No more tax dollars for war in Iran and genocide in Israel
issues.foreignpolicy_desc: No taxpayer dollars for forever war, apartheid and genocide. Byron will demand an end to taxpayer funded U.S. imperialism and redirect those billions toward our communities at home. Martin Luther King Jr. warned of the scourge of the three evils - poverty, racism, and militarism. Investing in global cooperation, global sustainability, and the education and health of our people is the pathway to a bright and sane future and we will build the coalition to win that future now.
issues.unbought_text: Byron completely rejects corporate PAC money and contributions from large real estate developers. He only answers to the working-class coalition of the 4th District. His campaign is funded by small-dollar donations from neighbors, teachers, union members, and working families. This is what it means to be truly independent.
issues.cta_headline: Fight for This Platform. Defend Your Choice.

machine.hero_sub: We are building an independent, working-class movement to defeat a corrupt political machine that believes it can govern without the consent of the people.
machine.movement_intro: Byron Sigcho-Lopez is an ideologically committed democratic socialist and a firebrand who has spent his entire career fighting for the multiracial working class. He is not a politician looking for a promotion. He is an organizer who was called to serve by his community.
machine.unbought_text: Unlike establishment politicians, Byron completely rejects corporate PAC money and contributions from real estate developers. His campaign is powered entirely by thousands of small-dollar grassroots donations from teachers, nurses, union members, and working families. He has upheld this commitment since his first campaign in 2015 and has never wavered.
machine.tested_text: Byron's unique power comes from bottom-up organizing. As 25th Ward Alderperson, he passed anti-displacement legislation to protect homeowners from predatory developers, created over 800 units of affordable housing, stood uncompromisingly with the Chicago Teachers Union, doubled the Affordable Requirements Ordinance minimum, and joined a hunger strike to fight environmental racism. These are not campaign promises. These are receipts.
machine.pullquote: "I have never taken a dollar from a corporation or a developer. I never will. My loyalty is to the people of this district, not to the machine."
machine.thesis: "Democracy cannot be preserved nationally if it is subverted locally."
machine.timeline_intro: What happened in IL-04 is not an isolated incident. It is part of a broader, dangerous pattern of the establishment insulating itself from the working class.
machine.timeline_2016: The DNC weaponized the undemocratic superdelegate system to block progressive momentum and override the will of grassroots voters.
machine.timeline_2020: The party establishment swiftly coalesced in a coordinated effort to block Bernie Sanders' grassroots movement, consolidating behind a single candidate overnight.
machine.timeline_2024: The party suppressed primary challenges and skipped debates, culminating in a late Biden drop-out and an uncompetitive process that left voters demoralized and demobilized.
machine.timeline_now: In IL-04, the same playbook is being used at the local level, handing a Congressional seat to a handpicked successor without a competitive election.
machine.cta_headline: They're Trying to Erase Your Choice. Fight Back.

volunteer.hero_headline: We Are The Machine's Worst Nightmare.
volunteer.hero_sub: We don't have corporate PAC money or backroom bosses. We have you. Join the multiracial working-class coalition to take back IL-04.
volunteer.blitz_p1: You did it. The law demanded 10,816 valid signatures from an independent, while the machine's candidate needed just 697. This movement collected and filed 22,788, more than double the requirement. The voters of IL-04 earned a choice on November 3rd.
volunteer.blitz_p2: Now the machine is trying to take it away. On June 9, 2026, machine lawyers filed an objection with the Illinois State Board of Elections to invalidate your signatures and kick Byron off the ballot, a process that could run into the first week of August. We beat them at the doors. Now we need you to spread the word: tell your neighbors, post the receipts, and expose what the machine is doing to our democracy.
volunteer.blitz_download: ✊ Join the Fight: Spread the Word
volunteer.canvass_desc: Knock on doors in Pilsen, Little Village, and the inner-ring suburbs to have meaningful, one-on-one conversations about housing, economic justice, and the fight against the machine. This is how movements are built: at the doorstep.
volunteer.ticket_desc: As an independent, Byron will not benefit from the straight-ticket Democratic vote. We need educators to teach voters how to split their ticket in November to defy the machine and cast a vote for a real representative.
volunteer.digital_desc: Reach voters where they are through rapid-response text campaigns, phone calls, and social media. This work can be done from anywhere, anytime, and is critical for expanding the movement beyond what door-knocking alone can achieve.
volunteer.precinct_desc: Lead the ground game in your neighborhood. Precinct captains coordinate local volunteers, organize neighbors to defend Byron's place on the ballot, and serve as the backbone of the campaign at the block level. Not selected? Support your captain however you can.
volunteer.creative_desc: Design flyers, create campaign videos, and push content across social media. From graphic design to videography and video editing, your creative skills can amplify Byron's message to thousands of voters.
volunteer.campus_desc: High school ambassadors and college campus captains help mobilize the next generation. Organize voter registration drives, host campus events, and build a youth coalition that fights for affordable education and a livable future.
volunteer.signup_desc: Fill out the form and our team will reach out with next steps. Whether you have one hour or one hundred, there is a role for you in this movement.

volunteer.cta_text: The machine is paying lawyers to throw out 22,788 signatures. Every dollar helps us defend the people's petitions at the Illinois State Board of Elections and keep your choice on the November ballot. This campaign is entirely unbought and funded by working people like you.

duel.r1_machine_text: Chuy Garcia filed for a fifth term, waited until the final hours before the deadline, then handed the seat to his former chief of staff. She needed 697 signatures. Voters got one choice.
duel.r1_movement_text: We are not waiting for the Democratic Party to give us permission. Byron announced in Pilsen at Cinco Estrellas, blocks from the classrooms where he taught.
duel.r1_movement_quote: "I do not build coalitions with politicians. I build coalition with my constituents."
duel.r2_machine_text: They publicly celebrated how secret the operation was, then introduced their candidate by playing in our faces about silencing our voices for another cycle.
duel.r2_movement_text: A reporter asked if an independent could even collect 10,816 valid signatures. The room answered before Byron could.
duel.r3_machine_text: Illinois election law demanded 10,816 valid signatures from an independent. Their candidate needed 697.
duel.r4_machine_text: This cycle in Illinois, $20 million from AIPAC, big tech oligarchs, and corporate interests denied people across the state the chance for fair elections.
duel.r4_movement_text: This campaign runs on 1,000 grassroots donations. Average gift: $27. No corporate PACs, no lobbyists, no AIPAC. Ever.
duel.r4_movement_quote: "It takes people and people defeats money."
duel.r5_machine_text: Machine lawyers are combing every line, challenging every misspelled name and every address one digit off, hoping to erase 22,788 voices one signature at a time, in a process built to drag into August.
duel.r5_movement_text: We are essential workers and we are going to fight back. Every volunteer who joins this fight is an answer the machine cannot object to. Let the people decide.

timeline.label: The Ballot Battle
timeline.headline: The Road to November
timeline.sigwall_label: signatures filed by volunteers. Every mark is a neighbor.
timeline.s1_desc: IL-04 voters got exactly one choice on the primary ballot. The machine chose on our behalf.
timeline.s2_desc: Byron announces in Pilsen. A reporter asks if 10,816 signatures is even possible. The room raises its hands and promises 20,000.
timeline.s3_desc: The movement files 22,788 valid signatures with the Illinois State Board of Elections, more than double the law's demand.
timeline.s4_desc: A machine-backed objector files a challenge to throw out your signatures and erase your choice.
timeline.s5_desc: Records exams and hearings at the State Board of Elections. The movement defends every line while machine lawyers try to strike them.
timeline.s6_desc: The Board rules on the challenge. This is the day we keep your choice alive.
timeline.s7_desc: Not the machine. Not the lawyers. You.
